status.work_note: Original seven-dimension anchor fully searched; earlier/modified implementations explicitly excluded from complete-form subsequent totals. See two schema issues; no identity conflict. STOPPING_RULE_MET: defining procedure, repeatability, diary/proxy comparison, recall bias, administration burden, windows and form/population limits deliberately checked. Further searches mainly repeat adaptations/applications and original validation citations. Recent synthesis and bias primary remain blocked and are explicit gaps; no exhaustive treatment-use census or generic alcohol TLFB search.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: 1 defining/development reference (1 programme) for the 2004 seven-dimension form; no subsequent complete-form primary programme retained in this bounded search. Separately retained: 1 earlier two-output gambling adaptation and 1 author-independent subsequent online two-output programme; 2 representative empirical applications of adapted forms. 2 relevant sources remain access-blocked.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
G-TLFB reconstructs gambling over a specified period using a calendar and meaningful dates. Its gambling-specific development study supports repeatability of several behavioural outputs and comparison with daily self-monitoring. These are separate outputs, including frequency, time and financial measures, rather than a single severity score.

The original evidence came from college gamblers. Strong correlations did not remove reporting differences: recalled frequency, own-money risk and alcohol use were lower than daily reports, and net financial outcomes showed weaker agreement. Both methods depended on self-report. Earlier gambling calendars and a later online gambler–collateral comparison provide useful supporting context, but used fewer outputs and different procedures.

The current search did not establish objective financial accuracy, a meaningful-change threshold or complete-form replication across clinical populations and administration modes. A recent treatment-outcome meta-analysis and a primary recall-bias study could not be read in full and are excluded from extracted evidence. Repeated use in treatment research therefore should not be read as validation of every shortened implementation or change score.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: State the recall window and calendar/event-aid procedure; shorter subsets of a longer calendar are not separately validated forms.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Distinguish intended stake, own money risked and net win/loss; these are not interchangeable expenditure measures.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Retrospective reports can differ from diaries; proxy agreement does not establish objective accuracy.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Completion burden varies with gambling frequency and detail; online or shortened procedures require their own evidence.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Behavioural change can be described, but meaningful-change thresholds and objective financial verification were not identified in the retained anchor evidence.

status.work_note: FAMILY_ANCHOR complete with bounded mature-literature search.5 primary study programmes/6publications; Canadian report/article grouped; four author-independent programmes. One blocked journal excluded. Four original/core applications plus one explicitly modified PGSI operationalisation. See schema issues.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Evidence currently identified: 1 defining/development source · 5 subsequent primary study programmes (6 full-text publications; 4 author-independent programmes) · 5 representative examples of use.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
The nine-item PGSI has substantial population-survey evidence for a coherent total severity score and consistent items. Selected Canadian and British studies include teams without Ferris/Wynne author overlap. Some publications reuse datasets; the retained counts describe this bounded search, not the entire literature. Ipsos corporate authorship does not establish individual independence.

Evidence is less clear for distinguishing the original low- and moderate-risk categories. Item interpretation, participation filters and sampling methods affect comparisons. Agreement with an older DSM-IV screen is not proof of DSM-5 diagnostic accuracy or a complete inventory of gambling harms.

Development-stage retest and later long-term stability/change analyses are available, but they do not establish an anchor-based meaningful-change threshold for the unchanged twelve-month form. Language adaptations, short forms and sports-specific versions require their own evidence; clinical application alone does not validate treatment responsiveness.

synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Short follow-ups may cover overlapping recall periods.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Keep severity categories distinct from diagnosis and a complete harm inventory.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Report participation filters, sampling and scoring changes when comparing studies.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Check exact-language, short-form and outcome-change evidence for the intended use.

status.work_note: Assigned standalone original 12-item object completed. Japanese MIC/Spanish revised-form context retained without original-form count or new variant objects. Singapore administration language not explicit. Source discrepancies, permissions and stale application-design validation logged. Family fields not applicable; no family row edited.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Evidence currently identified: 1 defining/development source · 1 subsequent primary study programme (1 publication; 1 author-independent programme) for the specified 12-item form · 3 representative examples of use.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
The original 12-item G-SAS assesses gambling symptoms over the previous week. Its developer-led US clinical study supports internal consistency and associations with clinician-rated severity. Changes in scores tracked clinician and global improvement ratings during treatment, although week-to-week stability was more modest. This evidence concerns recent symptoms in adults with gambling problems; it does not establish diagnostic accuracy or a complete inventory of gambling harms.

One retained subsequent programme, by authors outside the defining team, studied the specified 12-item scale in a Singapore treatment service. It supported consistent items and two related domains: impulses and adverse consequences. The sample was predominantly male and Chinese, and questionnaire administration language was not explicitly reported. Its results do not establish equivalence across languages, community populations or demographic groups.

Meaningful-change evidence retained from Japanese online self-help trials suggests a roughly four-point reduction over one week in that setting. This translated-form result is kept as context and is not a validated threshold for the original English form. A Spanish adaptation preferred an 11-item solution and is also kept separately from original-form claims. An original-form meaningful-change threshold and invariance evidence were not identified in the current bounded search.

Three representative examples show use in medication and psychological treatment research. One is within the development programme, and one reports severity classifications that differ from the defining paper. These applications demonstrate use rather than additional validation; publication, programme and dataset independence are distinct.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: State the 12-item form and previous-seven-day window; each visit covers recent symptoms rather than the whole interval between visits.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Use form- and language-specific evidence; the Spanish preferred 11-item model and Japanese change threshold do not automatically apply to the original form.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Treat symptom scores and descriptive severity bands separately from diagnosis and a complete assessment of harms.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Interpret change with the follow-up context and baseline symptoms in mind; original-form meaningful-change and measurement-error thresholds remain uncertain in this search.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Check scoring categories and questionnaire permissions: the hosted notice permits clinical practice and non-industry research, with other uses referred to the copyright owner.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: Standalone OBJECT, no family synthesis. One original-form subsequent programme counted; Japanese MIC and Spanish revised form are contextual only and excluded. Singapore administration language unresolved. Three representative applications include within-development use and one modified classification. Counts describe retained bounded search, not total literature. Source-specific discrepancies/provenance preserved.

status.work_note: Assigned original-task anchor complete. Two counted methodological programmes explicitly include computer/probe conditions; two later clinical programmes contextual only. PDW member incidental. STOPPING_RULE_MET: original specification, score definitions, independent repeatability/interpretation programmes, clinical-version practice/reliability context, three high-value syntheses, population caveats and representative gambling applications covered. Further duplicative applications unlikely to change public synthesis. No target gambling individual MDC/MCID or universal software equivalence identified; blocked source excluded. Stop after IGT; no CAL-A-01. CAL-I-01 closure: public specificity corrected to Generic / cross-domain; no P1C-A identity change.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Evidence currently identified: 1 defining/development reference (1 programme); 2 selected subsequent primary methodological programmes (2 publications; both author-independent) using original-payoff tasks, including an awareness-probe modification; 3 secondary syntheses; 1 representative anchor application. Two later clinical-version programmes are contextual evidence. This bounded selection is not a literature total.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
The IGT records choices from four decks while participants learn from gains and losses. Original development in people with focal brain lesions defined deck profiles and the advantageous-minus-disadvantageous net score. It provides evidence about decision behaviour under this task, rather than a direct gambling-harm measure or a test that uniquely isolates one mental process. Reward frequency, learning and knowledge of the decks can affect interpretation.

This bounded search retained two author-independent methodological programmes using original payoffs: a computer repeat-assessment study and an investigation with awareness probes. Raw performance showed limited repeat stability in the small student study; more stable computational parameters were different, model-dependent outputs. Two later clinical-version programmes are retained separately. Their weak score stability and practice effects should not be presented as coefficients for the original physical task.

Selected reviews show average IGT differences between gambling groups and controls, with variation in samples and task definitions. Such group associations do not establish individual diagnostic accuracy, causation of gambling harms or a unique latent construct. Healthy-adult synthesis also indicates population-related score differences. Evidence for universal comparability across software, payoff schedules, languages or populations was not established in this search.

Repeated exposure can improve performance without treatment. Individual reliable or meaningful change thresholds for gambling services were not identified in the current search. One retained gambling application illustrates use of the anchor task; post-decision wagering has separate, incidental adaptation evidence and its own scoring uncertainties. Only the anchor was fully searched.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Record payoff schedule, deck labels, software/version, instructions, incentives and trial count; later clinical and wagering versions need their own evidence.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: State whether the outcome is a net score, deck/block count or computational parameter; these outputs have different meanings.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Learning and repeat exposure can change performance; account for practice before interpreting treatment-related change.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Group differences do not establish individual diagnosis, gambling-harm attribution or one uniquely measured construct; consider reference-population comparability.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Administration and access resources depend on the implementation; this search does not establish equivalent software, norms or current licence terms.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: Counts describe bounded selected programmes, not an exhaustive census or independent datasets. Clinical programmes excluded from anchor counts; model parameters share one programme. ACCESS_BLOCKED candidate not counted. STOPPING_RULE_MET: original specification, score definitions, independent repeatability/interpretation programmes, clinical-version practice/reliability context, three high-value syntheses, population caveats and representative gambling applications covered. Further duplicative applications unlikely to change public synthesis. No target gambling individual MDC/MCID or universal software equivalence identified; blocked source excluded. Stop after IGT; no CAL-A-01.

Original development references remain blocked; development-reference list includes citation-only/context references with explicit qualifications. STOPPING_RULE_MET: original DSM-IV specification/provenance established through accessible secondary descriptions; two originating publications blocked. Two bounded interview programmes plus two explicitly separate self-report programmes cover consistency, convergence, structure, retest-context and administration limitations. No direct interviewer-agreement, independently referenced diagnostic accuracy or reliable/meaningful change estimate identified in this selection. Historical review and two representative applications retained. Further duplicative screen/use papers unlikely to materially alter the public synthesis; no DSM framework evidence transferred.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Current bounded selection: 2 subsequent interview-specific primary study programmes (2 publications), both author-independent of the original developers; 2 additional self-report programmes retained separately and excluded from interview counts; 1 historical synthesis; 2 representative applications. The original manual and developer chapter are access-blocked, so no directly retrieved original-development reference is counted. Programme counts do not imply independent datasets or validation of every recall-window implementation.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
DIGS is a clinician-administered interview that operationalises DSM-IV pathological-gambling criteria. Its original specification uses 20 questions paired across ten criteria, with five or more criteria indicating the DSM-IV diagnostic threshold. Accessible later descriptions explain the interview and scoring, but the original unpublished manual and developer chapter were not retrieved. This is an interview-specific evidence assessment; DSM criteria-framework evidence has not been assigned to DIGS.

Two selected studies provide direct evidence from trained-interviewer administrations in US college students and English-proficient South African gamblers. They report internal consistency and convergence with gambling screens or behaviour. The South African consistency result has an unresolved item-count discrepancy and needs caution. Neither study measured inter-rater agreement or compared DIGS against an independent clinical diagnosis; using DIGS as the reference for another screen does not establish DIGS diagnostic accuracy. Both author teams are independent of the original developers, but this does not establish dataset independence or broad generalisability.

Separate college studies examined participant-rated DIGS items and the computerised DIGS-S adaptation. These provide structural, consistency and repeat-assessment evidence for those implementations, rather than for the original clinician-rated interview. Lifetime self-report score changes also do not demonstrate responsiveness to treatment. The bounded search did not establish interview-specific measurement error, meaningful-change thresholds or equivalent performance across languages and settings.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Specify the diagnostic edition: the retained interview operationalises DSM-IV, including the five-of-ten rule; this is not automatic DSM-5 validation.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: State the recall window and score used. Original lifetime, past-year interview and combined current/lifetime implementations are not interchangeable.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Interview delivery requires trained rating judgement. Training descriptions do not substitute for measured agreement between interviewers.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Check which measure is being evaluated: screen accuracy against DIGS is not DIGS accuracy against an independent clinical diagnosis.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Computerised self-report adaptations, source inconsistencies and limited language/population coverage qualify interpretation; reliable or meaningful interview change was not established here.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: Structured diagnostic interview archetype complete at bounded calibration depth. OBJECT assignment has no public family; no family synthesis modified. Two eligible programmes are interview-specific past-year/current-lifetime implementations, not proof of every original lifetime form. Two adapted self-report programmes are excluded from original interview counts. Primary Table1 and source-specific operation preserved. CAL-I-01 closure approved P1C-A v1.1 correction: developer attribution changed from Anna E. synthesis.canonical_name: Iowa Gambling Task with post-decision wagering
synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Incidental coverage: 1 adaptation/development reference (1 programme) and 1 representative application, from the same paper. No separate full search or subsequent validation count.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
The Brevers adaptation adds a wager after choosing a deck and before seeing its outcome. Its gambling-group study explores post-decision wagering as an indicator of metacognitive self-awareness, while wagering may also reflect reward and loss preferences.

The primary paper reports source-specific advantageous-choice and wagering measures. MeasureGH therefore treats these as adaptation-specific outputs rather than automatically importing the canonical IGT advantageous-minus-disadvantageous net-score derivation. The source identifies Antoine Bechara among the developers/authors of the adaptation context. Canonical IGT evidence does not automatically validate this wagering operation.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Specify wager choices, timing relative to feedback, payoff schedule and advantageous-wager rule.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Wagering can reflect reward/loss preferences as well as awareness.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Use the Brevers source-specific advantageous-choice and wagering definitions; do not assume canonical IGT net-score equivalence.

status.work_note: Structured clinical/multi-domain assessment archetype complete at bounded calibration depth. OBJECT assignment has no public family; no family synthesis modified. One defining guideline, separate supporting tool-review and implementation context; no direct primary procedure evaluation retained. Application count1 is explicitly a non-empirical official service-audit resource, not an evaluated patient cohort. STOPPING_RULE_MET: official version, adult specialist-service purpose,17 assessment domains, medicine review, clinical outputs/workforce and guideline-development basis established. Systematic tool review inspected without transferring component evidence; official planning/audit resources retained. Targeted whole-procedure implementation/evaluation/feasibility/acceptability searches found no eligible direct empirical evaluation in the current search. Further generic screen/service-use papers unlikely to materially change this clinical-method public synthesis. Stop before WMH-CIDI and CSO DSM-IV; no other assignment started.

synthesis.canonical_name: NICE structured multi-domain assessment of gambling that harms
synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Current bounded selection: 1 authoritative defining guideline/specification (1 guideline-development context); 1 supporting systematic tool-evidence review; 0 retained empirical applications; 1 official implementation/audit resource. No subsequent primary study programme directly evaluating the complete multi-domain assessment was identified.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
NICE NG248 describes a structured clinical assessment for adults experiencing gambling-related harms in gambling treatment services. It brings together gambling history and patterns, health and mental-health concerns, suicide and safeguarding risk, financial and social harms, contributing factors, diagnostic alignment, motivation and immediate needs. Medication review is included. The information informs a collaborative formulation, care plan and safety plan when needed; the procedure does not produce a fixed questionnaire total or universal cut-off.

The guideline supplies an authoritative specification, but its multi-domain content was based on committee knowledge and experience. The supporting systematic review examined particular identification and assessment tools and found limited, very-low-quality accuracy evidence. Those tool studies do not directly evaluate the reliability, consistency or clinical effects of the complete NICE assessment. A validated severity tool or diagnostic framework can contribute to the assessment without validating the whole procedure.

Official implementation planning and a blank service-audit template are available. They support organising delivery but do not demonstrate uptake, acceptability, agreement between practitioners or improved patient outcomes. No eligible direct empirical evaluation of the complete procedure was identified in the bounded current search. This is an evidence-characterisation gap, rather than a claim that no evaluation exists or that the clinical approach lacks value.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Use the assessment to develop an individual clinical formulation and plan; it is not a summed psychometric scale or standalone severity endpoint.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Delivery requires competent staff, time and appropriate coordination for mental health, medicines, safety, safeguarding and practical needs.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Record current concerns alongside relevant history. The procedure has no single recall window or fixed interview wording, so local implementations may differ.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Specify any component questionnaire or diagnostic framework separately; its evidence and thresholds do not establish validity of the whole assessment.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: The official audit template is a planning resource. Direct evidence on the complete procedure’s consistency, feasibility, acceptability and outcomes was not identified in this search.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: Structured clinical/multi-domain assessment archetype complete at bounded calibration depth. The official audit/action-planning template is now classified separately as an IMPLEMENTATION_RESOURCE, not an empirical application. No direct primary whole-procedure evaluation retained. STOPPING_RULE_MET.

synthesis.canonical_name: Population-level attributable-fraction estimation of gambling-related harm costs
synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: 2 defining/development references (2 programmes; an additional companion guide shares the 2019 programme); 1 subsequent primary methodological programme (1 publication), author-independent; 1 broad secondary synthesis; 2 representative empirical applications; 1 implementation resource. Evidence supports specified excess-cost calculations, not universal causal PAF accuracy.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
This method combines population and gambling-exposure estimates with harm risks or excess case counts, then applies unit costs or health valuations. The originating OHID implementation compares expected harms in gambling-risk groups with a reference rate. Each harm domain has its own inputs and restrictions; the outputs are modelled cases and costs.

The defining reports explain a reproducible costing logic and the importance of transparent assumptions. A subsequent author-independent Finnish study directly compared alternative calculations on the same linked survey/register data and obtained substantially different estimates. A broad scoping review likewise identifies differences in included harms, exposure definitions, valuation and attribution. These findings characterise methodological sensitivity rather than establish one universally accurate estimator.

Associated excess costs should not automatically be interpreted as costs caused by gambling or savings achievable by removing it. Results depend on confounding, the reference group, risk transportability, data coverage and valuation. The OHID total combines government costs and valued health losses, excludes several harm categories and does not subtract gambling benefits. Cross-jurisdiction comparisons require matching scope, price year, population and time horizon.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Specify the gambling-exposure categories, reference population and counterfactual; causal PAFs and associated excess costs are different interpretations.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Check that prevalence and risk estimates match the target population; odds ratios, risk ratios and attribution proportions are not interchangeable.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: State the economic perspective, currency/price year, valuation and time horizon; distinguish fiscal transfers, resource costs and monetised health losses.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Report uncertainty and scenario choices; avoid adding overlapping harms or replacing costs twice.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Totals cover only included harms and populations. Differences across jurisdictions may reflect definitions and available data as well as burden.

synthesis.canonical_name: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition
synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Current bounded selection: 4 defining/development or specification references (one overlapping framework-development context); 5 subsequent primary gambling-criteria study programmes (5 publications); 2 narrative syntheses; 2 representative applications. Two primary programmes involve named developers; author independence of the other three is unclear, so no confirmed independent subset is reported. Original manual is access-blocked and excluded from extracted counts. This is not a literature total.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
DSM-5 is a diagnostic classification reference used to guide clinical assessment. For gambling disorder, the 2013 edition specifies nine criteria and a threshold of four within 12 months, alongside clinically significant impairment or distress and a manic-episode exclusion. It renamed and reclassified the disorder, removed the separate illegal-acts criterion, and added criterion-count severity and course/remission descriptions. Official development documents and an authoritative criteria reproduction support this specification; the original manual was not accessible in this search.

Five selected primary programmes examined gambling-criterion classification, reliability, structure or severity. Much of this evidence used older questionnaire or interview responses recoded to the DSM-5 rule. It supports the threshold changes in those implementations, with moderate short-term count stability and evidence of a common severity dimension. High agreement between editions comes from shared symptom data; classification against treatment status uses an imperfect reference. These results are not coefficients for the manual as an administered scale. Two programmes include named developers; independence from the full APA contributor team could not be confirmed for the other three. Reused cohorts also mean programme counts are not independent-dataset counts.

Criteria have different statistical severity and importance, and some function differently across gambling populations. Studies of severity bands found that moderate and severe cases did not consistently differ in functional impact; a recent Spanish clinical network study also found sex-related criterion patterns. Interviews and self-report questionnaires implementing the same criteria can classify different proportions. The inspected general DSM-5 field-trial report did not provide a gambling-specific agreement estimate, and evidence for universally equivalent assessment across settings or languages was not established here.

DSM-5 diagnosis provides a classification of disorder, rather than comprehensive coverage of gambling harms: harm can occur below its diagnostic threshold. A cross-sectional severity difference does not establish reliable or meaningful treatment change, and these criteria are not automatically a short-window outcome scale. This completed calibration anchor focuses on the gambling-disorder section, with component evidence recorded explicitly. It does not imply validation of every DSM-5 diagnosis or transfer evidence to DSM-IV, DSM-5-TR or other DSM versions.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: State the DSM edition and actual interview, questionnaire or clinical procedure; recoded DSM-IV responses do not directly test every final DSM-5 wording change.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: The diagnostic decision includes the 12-month window, impairment or distress and manic-episode exclusion; a bare symptom count or screen may omit these.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Classification concordance, clinician agreement and accuracy against an independent diagnosis answer different questions; check the reference used.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Criterion-count severity bands do not capture all gambling harms or automatically provide reliable or meaningful treatment-change thresholds.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Use requires clinical judgement and implementation-specific training/resources; consult authorised edition/access terms before reproducing criteria.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: Referenceframework archetype; bounded gambling sectionfocus, notwholemanual literaturecensus. Original manualcitationlistedbutexcludedcounts/extraction. Fiveprogrammeunion sharedwith0184; Molanderinstrument programme andgeneralfield trial excludedfromsubsequentpublic count. STOPPING_RULE_MET: official 2013definition/changes anddevelopmentrationale established; five boundedcriteria-focused programmes coverclassification/threshold, implementation-specific reliability, structure/DIF, severity andrecentpopulation/network limitations. Generalfield trials inspectedwithouttransferringotherdiagnoses; two narrativereviews andtwo representativeapplications retained. status.work_note: Bounded assigned anchor completed. Four syntheses cover large literature; two counted subsequent programmes plus two excluded German contexts. Limited gambling-specific alpha, no dedicated diagnostic/structural/retest validation identified. Derived members partial only; no PHQ4/SwedishPHQ8 search. STOPPING_RULE_MET: defining evidence and every requested domain covered by selected primary studies and four high-value syntheses; current error gap check added Wang2026. Further duplicative validation papers unlikely to change public conclusions: mature generic depression evidence; method/language/context qualifications; limited gambling-specific alpha only; endpoint/change need explicit specification. Review constituent studies not separately enumerated. Stop after one assigned unit; IGT untouched.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Evidence currently identified: 1 defining/development reference (1 programme); 2 retained subsequent primary programmes (2 publications; both author-independent) for the specified nine-item form; 4 secondary syntheses; 2 representative application examples. Two German contextual programmes are retained separately. This bounded selection is not a literature total.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
PHQ-9 measures depressive symptoms over the previous two weeks. Original clinical development and a large external evidence base support consistent items, expected relationships with functioning and useful depression-screening accuracy. A positive score needs clinical assessment; the questionnaire does not establish whether depression was caused by gambling. Structural reviews generally support a total score, with qualifications for analytical method and comparability across languages and time.

This calibration uses four selected syntheses and a small set of primary programmes, rather than counting the full literature. The two counted subsequent programmes have no defining-author overlap: UK primary-care change research and a Spanish telephone/retest study whose administration language was not explicitly reported. German responsiveness evidence is retained as translated-form context. Samples, reference interviews and administration modes affect interpretation; the counts do not establish independent datasets or English-language replication in every study.

PHQ-9 can track depression over time, but patient-perceived improvement and change beyond measurement error answer different questions. A recent pooled error analysis used internal consistency rather than observed retest change and found substantial variation across settings. Neither its pooled threshold nor a primary-care perceived-change estimate is a universal rule for gambling services. Endpoint and change scores need defined visits, sign, analysis and missing-data handling.

Two gambling-related examples illustrate use. A German slot-machine-gambler trial also reports limited sample-specific internal consistency; that result is retained separately from application evidence. Dedicated gambling-population diagnostic, structural and repeatability validation was not identified in the current bounded search. The Swedish example evaluates a gambling interview using PHQ-9 as a comparator, rather than validating PHQ-9 itself.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: State the nine-item form, language, mode and two-week recall window; shorter family members need their own evidence.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Screening thresholds and severity bands are different from a clinical diagnosis and from attributing depression to gambling.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Define endpoint visit and change-score sign, timepoints, estimand and missing-data method; questionnaire evidence does not settle every derived outcome.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Separate patient-important improvement from change beyond measurement error; threshold estimates depend on population and method.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Gambling-specific evidence identified here is limited; do not assume diagnostic accuracy or cross-language/time comparability in gambling services.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: Bounded FAMILY_ANCHOR search complete, not exhaustive. Two original-specification primary programmes counted; Spain language unreported. Independence NOT_APPLICABLE reflects lack of one developer team, not absence of independently authored work. Wewers blocked reference excluded from synthesis IDs. Official correction explicitly retained; no identity conflict. Bounded stopping: defining procedure, two broad methodological syntheses, two complementary direct response-format programmes, electronic implementation guidance and representative gambling use cover scaling, reliability context, comparability, change limitations and burden. Further construct-specific applications are unlikely to change this method-level synthesis; no exhaustive VAS census attempted.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Current bounded search: 1 defining reference; 2 subsequent primary study programmes (2 study papers plus 1 official correction); 2 full-text methodological syntheses; 2 representative empirical applications. One additional review is access-blocked and excluded. Author-independence counting is not applicable to this generic method.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
VAS is a response procedure: a person marks a position on an anchored continuous line, which is converted into a distance or proportional score. It can be configured for many constructs, but the wording, endpoints, reference period and scoring direction define each application. A continuous line does not itself establish equal psychological intervals or make scores comparable between different questions or people.

Methodological reviews and direct format comparisons show that carefully specified VAS can yield useful responses. Reliability, relationships with other rating formats and respondent burden vary with the question, population and implementation. Evidence for paper-to-electronic migration is most informative when presentation and response handling are preserved; arbitrary sliders or preset marks need separate consideration. No single reliability coefficient or meaningful-change threshold applies to VAS as a whole.

The change comparisons in the retained general response-format review concerned pain. They do not establish responsiveness for gambling harms or craving. A gambling-environment study illustrates use of a current-desire VAS, but use alone does not validate the method for gambling research. The retained primary programmes examine particular response formats and populations; generic VAS has no single developer team against which to interpret an independent-study count.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Specify the construct, exact question, endpoints, reference window and scoring direction for each VAS.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Keep paper dimensions or electronic line, device, marker and score conversion consistent; document format changes.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Correlated VAS, numeric and verbal scores may still differ for individuals or in their distributions.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Reliability, measurement error and meaningful change need evidence for the intended question and population.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Check that respondents can see, understand and use the line; a telephone numeric response is a different procedure.

status.work_note: Object-specific 2019 anchor; locked edition-unspecified label and construct preserved. No public family assigned.2025 context and official resources not counted as primary studies; no identity reopening. Minimum sufficient characterisation met:2019 defining edition,2011 LSOA geography,domains/weights/processing/QA,data-time limits and output interpretation; current official guidance covers 2025/boundary/nation incompatibility,lookup/aggregation and inequalities use; one direct 2019 income-proxy programme supports ecological limits; one exact-edition gambling application illustrates stratification. Additional health/gambling association papers would not validate the index or materially change the public synthesis. No exhaustive IMD validation or 2025 development review.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Bounded search anchored to IMD2019:1 defining/specification reference (1 construction programme);1 subsequent primary methodological programme (1 publication; author-independent);1 representative gambling application;3 official implementation resources. IMD 2025 is separate version context, not fully searched or included in 2019 programme counts.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
English IMD is a relative measure of neighbourhood deprivation. This evidence record anchors the 2019 release, which combines seven domains for England’s 2011 Lower-layer Super Output Areas. Published scores, ranks and groups describe the area: higher scores indicate more deprivation, while rank 1 and decile 1 identify the most deprived areas. Overall IMD and individual domains have different meanings.

The defining report documents input checks, statistical processing, internal audit and external scrutiny. A subsequent author-independent study linked IMD2019 to personal and household income and found limited proxy performance, varying across groups. This supports keeping area context separate from an individual’s circumstances. A gambling survey illustrates area stratification; its gambling findings are application evidence, not validation of IMD or proof of causation.

Edition, underlying data years, geographic boundaries and linkage files affect interpretation. The newer 2025 release uses changed inputs, methods and 2021 geography, so releases are not a simple time-series. Other UK nations publish distinct indices. For inequalities or adjusted analyses, specify grouping/aggregation and consider the health domain’s overlap with outcomes. Area deprivation cannot establish personal income, deprivation, gambling harm or causal effects.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: State the edition and input-data years, geographic vintage, lookup/remapping file and whether using overall IMD, a domain or a supplementary index. This record anchors 2019.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Keep score/rank/decile direction explicit: higher overall score means more deprived; rank 1/decile 1 most deprived. Rank gaps do not quantify deprivation differences.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Area context does not identify individual deprivation or income; linked analyses should acknowledge ecological interpretation and clustering.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Document national/local and area/population grouping plus aggregation; boundaries, releases and UK-nation indices are not directly interchangeable.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: For adjustment or inequalities analysis, justify edition and components, including health-domain overlap. Association with gambling does not establish index validity or causation.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: Object-specific 2019 anchor; locked edition-unspecified label and construct preserved. No public family assigned.2025 context and official resources not counted as primary studies; no identity reopening. Additional health/gambling association papers would not validate the index or materially change the public synthesis. No exhaustive IMD validation or 2025 development review.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Nested component coverage within DSM-5 anchor: 3 defining/specification references; the same 5 selected primary programmes, 2 narrative syntheses and 2 representative applications. No separate completed component search or additional family programme count; manual blocked.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
DSM-5 is a diagnostic classification reference used to guide clinical assessment. For gambling disorder, the 2013 edition specifies nine criteria and a threshold of four within 12 months, alongside clinically significant impairment or distress and a manic-episode exclusion. It renamed and reclassified the disorder, removed the separate illegal-acts criterion, and added criterion-count severity and course/remission descriptions. Official development documents and an authoritative criteria reproduction support this specification; the original manual was not accessible in this search.

Five selected primary programmes examined gambling-criterion classification, reliability, structure or severity. Much of this evidence used older questionnaire or interview responses recoded to the DSM-5 rule. It supports the threshold changes in those implementations, with moderate short-term count stability and evidence of a common severity dimension. High agreement between editions comes from shared symptom data; classification against treatment status uses an imperfect reference. These results are not coefficients for the manual as an administered scale. Two programmes include named developers; independence from the full APA contributor team could not be confirmed for the other three. Reused cohorts also mean programme counts are not independent-dataset counts.

Criteria have different statistical severity and importance, and some function differently across gambling populations. Studies of severity bands found that moderate and severe cases did not consistently differ in functional impact; a recent Spanish clinical network study also found sex-related criterion patterns. Interviews and self-report questionnaires implementing the same criteria can classify different proportions. The inspected general DSM-5 field-trial report did not provide a gambling-specific agreement estimate, and evidence for universally equivalent assessment across settings or languages was not established here.

DSM-5 diagnosis provides a classification of disorder, rather than comprehensive coverage of gambling harms: harm can occur below its diagnostic threshold. A cross-sectional severity difference does not establish reliable or meaningful treatment change, and these criteria are not automatically a short-window outcome scale. This completed calibration anchor focuses on the gambling-disorder section, with component evidence recorded explicitly. It does not imply validation of every DSM-5 diagnosis or transfer evidence to DSM-IV, DSM-5-TR or other DSM versions.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: State the DSM edition and actual interview, questionnaire or clinical procedure; recoded DSM-IV responses do not directly test every final DSM-5 wording change.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: The diagnostic decision includes the 12-month window, impairment or distress and manic-episode exclusion; a bare symptom count or screen may omit these.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Classification concordance, clinician agreement and accuracy against an independent diagnosis answer different questions; check the reference used.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Criterion-count severity bands do not capture all gambling harms or automatically provide reliable or meaningful treatment-change thresholds.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Use requires clinical judgement and implementation-specific training/resources; consult authorised edition/access terms before reproducing criteria.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: PARTIAL_EVIDENCE nested componentonly. Exact empiricalfindings attributedhere; parent0109providesframeworkcontext. Noautomaticvalidationofeveryimplementingtool orchangeoperation.

status.canonical_name: World Mental Health Composite International Diagnostic Interview
status.work_note: Named historical gambling evidence anchor within locked version-unspecified WMH-CIDI0293; no identity/type/construct remapping. Draft remains module-stratified. STOPPING_RULE_MET: authoritative definition/module, mode/edition/recall/algorithms, landmark psychiatric agreement, explicit gambling consistency/gap, modified-gate sensitivity and two representative applications cover the public synthesis. Further broad CIDI validation or application accumulation is unlikely to change it; no exhaustive census. Gambling retest/inter-rater/clinical accuracy remain not identified in this bounded search.

synthesis.canonical_name: World Mental Health Composite International Diagnostic Interview
synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Current bounded anchor search: 2 defining/specification references in 1 development context; 2 subsequent primary programmes (2 publications; 0 author-independent): 1 psychiatric-module clinical reappraisal and 1 gambling-module consistency programme. One independent modified-form programme retained separately; 2 representative gambling applications. No gambling clinical-accuracy programme identified in this search.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
WMH-CIDI is a fully structured psychiatric interview administered by trained interviewers. For gambling, the evidence here concerns the DSM-IV CIDI3.0 module used in the US National Comorbidity Survey Replication and its posted schedule. It gathers lifetime symptom history and recency alongside gambling behaviour and treatment information. It is not a single summed severity scale.

The gambling symptom reports showed good internal consistency in the US survey, but the authors explicitly reported no clinical reappraisal of gambling diagnoses. A landmark clinical comparison supports agreement for named anxiety, mood and substance modules; those results do not establish gambling diagnostic accuracy. Both anchor measurement programmes involved developers, and their US components share the parent survey.

German PAGE research illustrates translated, modified telephone administration and shows why screening gates matter: restrictive loss gates could miss criterion-positive participants. That evidence concerns the modified implementation. Exact release, wording, diagnostic algorithm, reference period and population therefore matter. Gambling-specific repeatability and diagnostic-accuracy evidence were not identified in the current bounded search.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Specify the WMH-CIDI release, gambling module, language, administration mode and diagnostic edition; CIDI short forms and other versions have separate evidence.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Lifetime criteria, recent symptoms and gambling-behaviour outputs are different operationalisations; retain the exact algorithm and mania exclusion.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Screening gates, optional-module sampling and weights affect who is assessed and how population estimates are interpreted.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Clinical agreement for other psychiatric modules does not validate the gambling module; alpha does not establish diagnostic accuracy or retest stability.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Historical training/certification and permission requirements apply to the posted materials; check current access and support for the intended release.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: Named historical gambling evidence anchor within locked version-unspecified WMH-CIDI0293; no identity/type/construct remapping. Draft remains module-stratified. STOPPING_RULE_MET: authoritative definition/module, mode/edition/recall/algorithms, landmark psychiatric agreement, explicit gambling consistency/gap, modified-gate sensitivity and two representative applications cover the public synthesis. Further broad CIDI validation or application accumulation is unlikely to change it; no exhaustive census. Gambling retest/inter-rater/clinical accuracy remain not identified in this bounded search.

status.work_note: Evidence calibration complete; public draft requires identity adjudication before publication. Exact affected-other form retained. P1CA_REOPENING_CANDIDATE P1CB-ISSUE-000039. STOPPING_RULE_MET: original accessible item specification, corroborating appendix, originating citation/access attempts, two qualified representative applications and high-value affected-other review cover the public synthesis. Further application accumulation is unlikely to resolve scoring/edition/proxy-accuracy gaps. No exact-form subsequent primary agreement/accuracy/retest programme identified in this bounded search; reopen specification rather than invent scoring. Stop before CAL-M-01. CAL-A-01 closure approved P1C-A v1.2 correction: original accessible form is eight lifetime/ever questions with four response categories; developer spelling/citation corrected to Nicole Peden and the 2002 brief-intervention article. Original-form numeric recoding/cut-off remains not established; later /10 and four-criterion operationalisations remain separate/unresolved.

synthesis.canonical_name: Concerned Significant Other DSM-IV Screening Questionnaire
synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Current bounded search: 1 accessible defining reference in 1 development programme; 1 originating journal publication ACCESS_BLOCKED and excluded from extracted evidence. No subsequent primary measurement programme identified; 1 secondary review; 2 representative collateral-assessment applications, with later-form equivalence unresolved.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
This assessment asks a concerned significant other about the gambler, rather than asking the gambler directly. The accessible original thesis and the later trial report reproduce an eight-question DSM-IV collateral screen with four response categories (Definitely true, Probably true, Not true, Unsure) and ever/lifetime wording. The MeasureGH identity has been corrected to that source-backed specification.

The accessible original form does not establish a validated numeric recoding rule or cut-off. Later studies use a four-criterion probable-case rule and/or report a ten-criterion DSM-IV-TR score, but equivalence to the original eight-question form is not established. Use for eligibility or stratification does not establish diagnostic accuracy. The originating 2002 journal article remains inaccessible; defining extraction therefore comes from the full 2001 thesis, with the 2004 report corroborating the questionnaire form.

A recent affected-other review helps bound the literature. Direct agreement with clinician diagnosis or gambler reports, test–retest reliability and diagnostic classification performance for the exact original form were not identified in the current bounded search. Proxy observations, relationship context and unresolved later scoring operationalisations therefore matter when interpreting results.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Use the original eight-question/four-response specification unless a later operationalisation is explicitly intended; do not assume a validated 0–8/0–10 score or four-criterion cut-off for the original form.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Record the CSO relationship, contact and information access: proxy reports are a distinct perspective, not direct gambler or clinician diagnosis.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: The original items use ever/lifetime wording; current behavioural windows from companion measures do not change that recall period.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Response recoding, Unsure handling and the four-criterion probable-case rule require explicit justification; direct accuracy evidence was not identified.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Keep DSM-IV/DSM-IV-TR dependence explicit. DSM-5 evidence and reliability of other collateral measures do not automatically apply.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: CAL-A-01 closure approved P1C-A v1.2 identity/specification correction. Evidence work COMPLETE; later ten-criterion and four-threshold operationalisations remain source-specific rather than silently merged.

status.work_note: Object-specific evidence complete; public DRAFT pending identity adjudication. No public family assigned; related forms are explicitly limited contextual/modified evidence. P1CB-ISSUE-000054 Minimum sufficient characterisation reached for the preserved locked estimand: debit direction/positive outflow magnitude,90-day requirement, observed versus derived features, source-specific mapping/windows/coverage, merchant audit and missing payment channels, bank-population differences, comparability and harm limits documented. Exact 90-day performance remains unestablished; originating citation conflict logged for adjudication. More association papers are unlikely to change the public synthesis or resolve that identity decision. Stop without surveying variants. CAL-N-01 closure approved P1C-A v1.3 correction: canonical merchant outflow remains gross gambling-merchant debit outflow, but the fixed 90-day GC2024 provenance is removed. Zendle & Newall 2024 supplies direct gross-outflow specification; GC2024 91-day debit-minus-credit net deposits remain contextual evidence.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Bounded search:1 specification/feasibility reference for a related outflow form (1 programme);1 subsequent primary data-quality programme (1 publication, annual form);3 representative applications. No direct validation of the locked 90-day gross-outflow form identified. Author-independence comparison is not applicable to this generic indicator; originating citation conflict awaits adjudication.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
Bank-transaction-derived gambling merchant outflow sums outgoing transactions classified as gambling-related over a stated observation window. The indicator is therefore a gross account-flow measure. It is distinct from net deposits (debits minus credits), operator turnover, realised gambling loss, affordability and gambling harm.

The current MeasureGH identity is anchored to direct bank-transaction studies that separately identify outgoing gambling expenditure, including Zendle and Newall's one-year open-banking analysis. The Gambling Commission's 2024 threshold-modelling report is retained as related evidence because it uses open-banking data and merchant classification, but its principal estimand is debit minus credit net deposits over 91 calendar days; it does not define the gross-outflow indicator.

Coverage depends on the connected bank accounts, merchant classification, payment channels and transaction-processing rules. Cash, other accounts, e-wallets, intermediaries, mixed retailers, refunds/reversals and classification drift can all alter the observed total. Associations between merchant outflow and PGSI, financial stress or other outcomes demonstrate application, not diagnostic accuracy or causal harm measurement.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: State the exact observation window, transaction direction, merchant-classification rule, account/provider coverage and currency; do not substitute net deposits or net gambling loss for gross merchant outflow.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Report connected banks/accounts and omitted cash, wallets, intermediaries, mixed retailers or other people’s cards; one bank is not a complete personal gambling record.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Keep incoming gambling payments and credits separate from gross debits. State reversal, refund, transfer and duplicate-handling rules rather than assuming netting.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Distinguish observed transactions from binned sums, spending ratios and model features; selected merchant audits do not supply universal classification accuracy.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Compare periods and banks only with compatible coding and coverage. Outflow alone does not establish losses, affordability, harm or diagnosis.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: CAL-N-01 closure approved the P1C-A v1.3 provenance/specification correction. Gross merchant debit outflow remains the canonical indicator; GC2024 net-deposit threshold modelling is related contextual evidence, not the defining form.

status.public_family_name: Gambling treatment engagement and retention indicators
status.work_note: Anchor0519 complete. Defining reviews/guidance are non-primary specification, not development validation programmes. Source/programme overlap explicit; generic author independence NOT_APPLICABLE. One new service-manifest schema issue; no identity reopening. Minimum sufficient characterisation met: defining treatment-flow/eligibility logic, multiple completion rules, rate heterogeneity, one direct early-response classification programme, observed administrative exit/ongoing reporting and contemporary review cover consequential interpretation and comparability. Direct coding reliability, comprehensive transfer/pause/death/re-entry handling and standardised censoring are not identified in current search; gaps recorded rather than invented. Further predictor/application accumulation is unlikely to change this public synthesis; no census or attendance-member search.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Current bounded search:2 defining/reporting references (including1 review);1 subsequent primary methodological programme (1 publication);2 overlapping secondary syntheses;2 representative applications;1 implementation resource. Author-independence comparison is not applicable to this generic service indicator; reviewed studies are not additional extracted programmes.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
Treatment dropout rate describes a source-defined proportion of people or treatment episodes ending before an expected endpoint. Services may define this through missed sessions, a minimum attendance rule, completion of a planned course or clinical judgement. Entry at referral, intake or the first treatment session also creates different denominators.

Two retained reviews show substantial variation in definitions and reported rates. Their overlapping evidence should not be added together as independent primary studies. A selected primary analysis found that some clients leaving an initial six-session block had already improved in depression; this does not establish sustained gambling recovery, but it shows why attendance alone can misclassify clinical progress.

Routine reporting can separate unscheduled exits from completed care, referrals, other discharges and episodes still open. A proportion among closed episodes differs from the chance of dropping out among all treatment starters. Direct exit-coding reliability and universal rules for pauses, transfers, re-entry, deaths or follow-up were not identified in this bounded search.

The indicator describes service engagement or process under its stated rules. It cannot establish why a person left, whether they recovered or the quality of care without additional information. Lower rates are not automatically better care, and comparisons require similar cohorts, endpoints, follow-up and coding.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: State numerator, denominator, treatment-entry rule and expected endpoint; distinguish referral/intake attrition, during-treatment dropout and follow-up non-response.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Specify observation period, episode construction and handling of ongoing care/censoring; closed-episode percentages differ from starter-cohort risks.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Record voluntary versus service-initiated exits and separate transfer, agreed early completion, pauses/re-entry, deaths and administrative discharge where the data permit.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Document missing/unknown exit codes, duplicate episodes and service coverage; do not assume coding reliability from review-screening agreement.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Interpret completion alongside goals, symptom change and patient/service context; the rate alone supplies neither reasons for leaving nor a care-quality ranking.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: Anchor0519 complete. Defining reviews/guidance are non-primary specification, not development validation programmes. Source/programme overlap explicit; generic author independence NOT_APPLICABLE. One new service-manifest schema issue; no identity reopening. Direct coding reliability, comprehensive transfer/pause/death/re-entry handling and standardised censoring are not identified in current search; gaps recorded rather than invented. synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Current bounded search:2 defining/specification references (1 empirical development programme);3 subsequent primary methodological programmes (3 publications);2 representative applications;2 implementation resources. Author-independence comparison is not applicable to this generic indicator; counts are not a literature census.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
Net money lost is a monetary quantity calculated over a stated period. The retained sources use cash-based reconstruction, retrospective reports and operator-recorded bets minus winnings. An annual loss divided by12 is an average month, rather than a direct observation of the last month. Account deposits minus withdrawals measures a different cash flow.

Direct comparisons show that wording, recall, spending intensity, product mix and data cleaning affect self-reported estimates. Operator records provide a comparison within their covered accounts and products; they do not automatically cover gambling elsewhere. Proxy reports are also imperfect. Agreement findings belong to the particular source, window and reporting procedure studied.

Loss distributions can be highly skewed, and changing the treatment of extreme values or winnings can change summaries. Absolute loss describes money, rather than affordability, financial harm or gambling disorder. Clinical associations do not establish accuracy or a harm threshold. This bounded search provides methodological examples across survey, operator and treatment settings; it does not validate every financial family variant or accounting convention.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Specify formula, sign convention, currency, price basis, observation window and whether the output concerns a person, account, activity, household or population.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Report product/account coverage and handling of bonuses, free bets, cash-outs, refunds, transfers, unsettled bets and balances; unspecified rules are evidence gaps.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Distinguish stakes minus winnings from turnover, deposits minus withdrawals and income-normalised ratios; annual-average and directly observed monthly loss differ.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Describe recall aids, missingness, zeros/winnings and outlier handling; correlation with records does not guarantee agreement.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Interpret loss alongside resources and consequences when relevant; monetary loss alone does not measure harm, affordability or diagnosis.

synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Current bounded search: 2 authoritative defining/specification references sharing NICE policy (0 empirical development programmes); 3 subsequent primary methodological programmes in 3 publications, including 1 utility-input comparison; 3 guidance resources; 1 representative empirical gambling application. Author-independence comparison not applicable. 1 access-blocked candidate excluded; metadata-only review not counted.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
QALYs combine time lived with a preference-based value for health-related quality of life. They can describe accrued health, or a gain/loss relative to a stated comparator. The metric is separate from the questionnaire and value set used to supply utilities, and from costs, decision thresholds and other burden measures.

The retained methodological evidence supports careful calculation and interpretation: utility instruments may yield different values, baseline differences can alter incremental estimates, and missing-data assumptions can change results. Study calculations and lifetime projections require different assumptions. Death is the zero anchor; negative health-state values are possible, and the horizon, survival handling, interpolation and discount policy must be explicit.

One gambling feasibility trial calculated QALYs over six months from repeated EQ-5D measurements. It demonstrates use, rather than validated gambling-specific responsiveness or established intervention benefit. Attributing utility losses to gambling also requires a justified counterfactual, confounding control and a duration assumption; a cross-sectional utility association alone cannot establish that loss. The retained HSE study provides a caution about such attribution, while one candidate loss study remains inaccessible.

The search is a bounded methodological characterisation, not a census or historical account of QALY development. NICE guidance provides the specification; its August 2026 interim value-set statement overrides older manual passages. The historical trial mapping remains recorded as performed. There is no single QALY developer team for the author-independence comparison.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: State whether the result is accrued QALYs or a gain/loss, and name the comparator and sign convention.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Name the utility instrument, version, value set and population; values from different instruments are not automatically interchangeable.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Report measurement times, interpolation, survival/death handling, baseline adjustment and missing-data assumptions; negative utilities are possible.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Separate within-study calculations from projected QALYs, and state the horizon, discounting and uncertainty analysis.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Gambling-attributed losses need a defensible counterfactual and duration. Health utility does not capture every financial, social or affected-other harm.

synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
Group model building brings stakeholders and facilitators together to make views of a system explicit and examine possible actions. Scripts can produce causal-loop diagrams, stock-flow structures, simulations or priorities. The chosen procedure determines the output; there is no single questionnaire, score or invariant set of constructs.

Methodological guidance and a review describe potential benefits for learning, communication and agreement. Evaluation remains sensitive to context, facilitation and the chosen tools; small studies and self-reported learning limit stronger claims. The retained community process programme shows how maps were revised with participants and how sustained partnership mattered for subsequent action. Its authors helped implement the process, and author independence against a single GMB developer team cannot be established.

A clearly documented gambling-specific GMB application was not identified in the current bounded search. Neighbouring participatory systems-mapping work was not treated as equivalent. Participant agreement about a causal link makes a shared hypothesis visible; it does not quantitatively verify causation or guarantee that an intervention will work.

synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
The defining framework proposes reconstructing an individual’s gambling-related harms across their life and, where feasible, estimating associated costs. It allows interviews, surveys or longitudinal data rather than prescribing a standard interview or costing schedule. The retained object is a configurable case-study design.

Generic case-study and gambling-costing guidance support transparent boundaries, multiple evidence sources and explicit attribution and valuation assumptions. The current search did not identify a completed primary evaluation of the full gambling-specific procedure. Adjacent examples show participant narrative reconstruction and record-based institutional costing, but support only those components and contexts.

A case account can illuminate a pathway and reveal costs omitted from aggregate records. Narrative evidence, observed service use, imputed quantities and monetised estimates need separate reporting. An individual estimate does not establish population prevalence, average harm costs or a causal effect; the missing fixed protocol limits comparison between implementations.

Original primary programmes include computational experiments, not clinical validation. Three schema/provenance issues retained. Synthesis draft for calibration adjudication. Bounded stopping rule met: definition/design, relationship-report reliability/error, sampling/boundary/missingness, metric sensitivity, temporal representation, causal interpretation, reproducibility/confidentiality and burden searched. Three scoped reviews, selected original methodological programmes and two gambling applications sufficiently characterise consequential choices. synthesis.evidence_currently_identified_line: Current bounded search:1 defining methodological exposition;3 subsequent primary methodological programmes (3 papers/reports, including2 simulation programmes);3 secondary syntheses;2 representative gambling applications;2 implementation resources. Author-independence comparison is not applicable to this generic method; these are retained-source counts, not a census.
synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
Social network analysis describes relationships among people, organisations or other specified actors. A study defines who belongs in the network, what each relationship means, how it is recorded and over what period. Outputs can describe immediate connections, paths, overall connectedness or local groups. Whole-network and ego-network designs provide different views; SNA has no fixed questionnaire, universal total score or single latent construct.

Methodological reviews and selected primary studies show that results depend on data coverage and design. Recall, nomination limits, non-response and missed relationships can alter the network and its measures. Reliability estimates belong to particular data-collection procedures and outputs. Simulations demonstrate sensitivity to errors and misleading causal patterns, but their assumptions do not provide universal error tolerances for real networks.

Networks can change over time. Aggregating contacts may lose their order, and apparent change can combine real turnover with reporting differences. Similar behaviour among connected people does not by itself establish social influence; selection and shared causes require consideration. Transparent definitions, data handling, analysis code and contextual interpretation support reproducibility. Specialist design and analytical skills, respondent workload and confidentiality need planning.

Two retained gambling studies illustrate ego-network applications using different contact-selection rules. They demonstrate use, rather than validation of a universal SNA procedure or gambling-harm score. This bounded search characterises core methodological choices; it does not cover every algorithm, population or application. There is no single developer team against which to classify author independence.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Specify actors, boundaries, relationship meaning, direction, weights, time window and whether the design is whole-network or egocentric.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Document missing nodes/ties, non-response, nomination limits and how conflicting reports are handled; an unobserved tie need not be an absent tie.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Choose measures for the question and report normalisation, thresholds, software/algorithm settings and sensitivity checks; similar labels need not mean comparable outputs.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Repeated or temporally ordered data can change interpretation; network association or change alone does not establish a causal influence or intervention effect.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Plan respondent burden, specialist analysis and confidentiality, including information about contacts who have not themselves participated.
synthesis.synthesis_author_note: Object-only broad-method coverage; no public family exists in locked mapping. Generic configurable design explained without altering DEFINED/C1903. Original primary programmes include computational experiments, not clinical validation. Three schema/provenance issues retained. Synthesis draft for calibration adjudication. Bounded stopping rule met: definition/design, relationship-report reliability/error, sampling/boundary/missingness, metric sensitivity, temporal representation, causal interpretation, reproducibility/confidentiality and burden searched. Three scoped reviews, selected original methodological programmes and two gambling applications sufficiently characterise consequential choices. Follow-on searches mainly produced already represented reviews, applications or construct-variable networks; further census unlikely to materially change this public synthesis. Specific algorithms, new metrics and other canonical units not pursued.

synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
GAMTOMS combines client assessments at admission, discharge and follow-up with a record of treatment services. It gathers gambling, financial/legal, mental-health, substance-use and recovery information to support treatment monitoring and service evaluation. It produces domain-specific information rather than one overall package score. The specification characterised here is the 2007 questionnaire/interview package, with DSM-IV gambling content; the earlier Minnesota application used a different battery.

The defining paper reports two developer-led cohorts, one for each administration form. It provides expert content review, short-term reliability and validity results for selected components, plus comparison of service records with charts. Some components performed less consistently than others. These findings support particular outputs and time points; they do not establish one reliability coefficient, diagnostic accuracy estimate or meaningful-change threshold for the whole package.

Observed changes and the earlier service application show how the system can be used for monitoring. Follow-up availability, self-report and proxy substitutions need careful interpretation, and improvement in an uncontrolled study does not establish a treatment effect. Samples were limited mainly to White Minnesota treatment clients. Independent integrated-package evaluation, interview inter-rater agreement, direct mode comparison and current electronic-version evidence were not identified in this bounded search. A current full manual/form set was not obtained; the retained public appendix is a specification resource.
synthesis.things_to_consider_1: Identify the package revision, component forms and diagnostic edition; early and 2007 batteries differ.
synthesis.things_to_consider_2: Keep each component’s score, reference window and evidence separate; there is no validated overall GAMTOMS total.
synthesis.things_to_consider_3: Allow for client and staff time at admission/discharge and for tracing follow-up participants.
synthesis.things_to_consider_4: Report who was due for follow-up, who responded, unknown outcomes and any proxy or substitute data.
synthesis.things_to_consider_5: Confirm access to the intended forms/manual and scoring procedures; current electronic versions and licence conditions were not verified.

synthesis.public_evidence_narrative:
Most Significant Change collects accounts of changes that participants consider important, then makes stakeholder selection and interpretation explicit. Its useful outputs are stories, reasons for significance and learning about a programme, rather than a standard recovery score. The foundational sources describe the general method; a fixed gambling-recovery implementation was not identified in the current search.

Developer-led experience, a separate Laos evaluation and a health practice review show how collection, deliberation, feedback and verification can support reflective evaluation. They also expose selective reporting, unequal voice, translation and staff-time demands. These sources provide methodological context rather than direct evaluation of the retained recovery application. Author independence of the Laos report does not establish independence from all material discussed in the development guide.

Selected stories can illuminate unexpected changes and participant values. They cannot show how common a change is, the average recovery outcome or the effect caused by treatment. Triangulation and clear documentation of the local procedure remain central.
